headline: Argentine Country Risk Surpasses 800 Points as Bonds and Equities Fall
summary: Argentine country risk exceeded 800 basis points for the first time in a year as bonds dropped, the MSCI Merval index fell 3.2%, and the central bank did not purchase reserves.
why: Emerging market sovereign debt and country risk spreads reflect investor confidence in a nation's fiscal solvency, macroeconomic stability, and debt servicing capacity.

entities.name: Banco Central de la República Argentina

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Rising country risk and falling bond prices signal deteriorating investor confidence in the nation's financial assets.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Regional reactions, uncertainties surrounding 2027 financing, and a slower pace of official foreign currency purchases pressured Argentine sovereign bonds and pushed risk metrics higher.
